documents.title: Sodium result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Irene - your sodium on Friday was 130. Not normal yet, but steady, and that's what we want with SIADH. Keep up the fluid limit (about 5 cups a day, soups and coffee included). We'll check it again when I see you in February. Any headache, unsteadiness or muddled thinking - call us the same day.

documents.title: RE: Sodium result
documents.author: patient
documents.body: OK. The coffee is the hard part. Infusion went fine last week.

documents.title: Follow-up - COPD, SIADH
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Doing ok. Breathing at baseline since December, albuterol a few times a week. Atezolizumab q4wk continues, last 2/2. Had her scan in January - she says the oncologist told her it "still looks good, no growth." No letter from oncology here; requested. Fluid restriction: honest that she slips, especially tea in the afternoon. No headache, no falls, thinking clear.

O: Vitals per flowsheet. Alert, conversational, appropriate. Lungs diminished, no wheeze or crackles. RRR. No edema.

Labs: Na 128 today (130 in Jan, 131 in Dec).

A/P
1. SIADH - drifting down a little. Tightened to 1 L/day; wrote it out for her and for her daughter. Will recheck in about a month. If it keeps sliding, will talk with oncology about salt tablets or other options.
2. COPD GOLD 3 - stable. Continue tiotropium, fluticasone, PRN albuterol.
3. ES-SCLC - on maintenance; Jan restaging reportedly stable; awaiting report.
RTC 4-6 wks with BMP.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet (1 g) by mouth three times daily with meals

reports.text: Noncontrast CT of the head. Indication: confusion, small cell lung cancer. No intracranial hemorrhage. No mass, mass effect or midline shift. No acute territorial infarct. Ventricles and sulci normal for age. Gray-white differentiation preserved. Visualized paranasal sinuses and mastoids clear.
reports.conclusion: No acute intracranial abnormality. No mass.

documents.title: ICU and Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: critical care medicine
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted via the ED to the medical ICU 03/07/2026; transferred to the floor 03/09; discharged home 03/12/2026.

Principal diagnosis: Severe symptomatic hyponatremia due to SIADH.
Other: Extensive-stage small cell lung cancer on maintenance atezolizumab. Severe COPD. SIADH first diagnosed 12/2025 (admission for COPD exacerbation and pneumonia).

Presentation: 73-year-old woman brought in by her daughter for two days of confusion and sleepiness. The daughter noticed her mother answering slowly and less engaged, and says she had been eating and drinking very little for about a week.

Exam: vital signs stable. Oriented to self only - not to place or date. Mucous membranes moist, no orthostatic findings, no sign of dehydration. Non-focal neurological exam.

Data: serum Na 120, serum osmolality 260, urine Na 45, urine osmolality 500. CT head: no acute abnormality, no mass. TSH 1.8, AM cortisol 14.2 (adrenal and thyroid causes excluded, relevant on immunotherapy).

Course: ICU admission for symptomatic hyponatremia. 3% saline with sodium checks every 2-4 hours; correction limited to no more than 8 mEq/L in 24 hours. Na 120 -> 125 at 24 h -> 128 (3/10) -> 130 (3/12). Mentation back to baseline by 3/9, transferred to the floor. Low solute intake over the preceding week likely contributed on top of SIADH. Oncology consulted; continue atezolizumab on schedule.

Discharge medications:
- NEW: sodium chloride 1 g tablet PO three times daily with meals
- Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaled daily
- Fluticasone propionate 250 mcg inhaled BID
- Albuterol HFA PRN
- Ondansetron 8 mg PO q8h PRN
- Atezolizumab per oncology

Instructions: fluid restriction 1 L per day. Eat regular meals with salt. BMP within one week with PCP. Return for confusion, drowsiness, falls or seizure.
Allergies: NKDA.
Condition at discharge: alert and oriented x3, ambulating independently.

documents.title: Call from Daughter
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Daughter (HCP) called. Mom was admitted Saturday 3/7 - she found her confused and sleepy, took her to the ED; sodium was 120 and she went to the ICU. They've been giving her a special IV salt solution. Today she knows where she is again and is moving to a regular floor. Hospital hasn't sent us anything.
Told daughter we'd like to see her mom within a week of discharge and to bring the discharge papers. Message to PCP. Records request faxed to the hospital.

documents.title: PCP Note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Spoke with the ICU team by phone - sodium 125 by yesterday afternoon, careful correction, mentation better. Likely home later this week. Front desk to hold a TCM slot.

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM. With daughter. Hospitalized 3/7-3/12, ICU 3/7-3/9, for symptomatic hyponatremia (Na 120) from her SIADH. Discharge summary not yet received; reviewed the patient's discharge paperwork the daughter brought (med list, instructions, last Na 130 on 3/12). Contact with family 3/9 and 3/13.

S: Feels like herself. Remembers little of the first day. Eating 3 meals, adding salt. Taking the salt tablets with meals. Drinking to 1 L, daughter checking. No headache. No falls.

Med rec: NEW sodium chloride 1 g TID added to our list. Tiotropium, fluticasone, albuterol PRN, ondansetron PRN unchanged. Atezolizumab q4wk per oncology - next 3/30.

O: Vitals per flowsheet. Alert, oriented x3, conversational, recalls 3/3 words. Gait steady. Lungs diminished, no wheeze. RRR. No edema.

A/P
1. SIADH with severe symptomatic hyponatremia, recovering. BMP today. Salt tablets 1 g TID, restriction 1 L/day. Recheck in 4 wks. Low threshold for the ED for any confusion.
2. Extensive-stage SCLC - maintenance atezolizumab; oncology aware of admission.
3. COPD - stable.
Addendum 15:20: Na 131. Daughter informed by phone.

documents.title: BMP Result Note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Na 133 on salt tabs + 1 L restriction - best since November. Rest of BMP fine. ICU discharge summary finally arrived 4/2, consistent with what the family brought; scanned. Message to pt: no changes.

reports.text: CT chest, abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast. Comparison 01/20/2026 and 10/28/2025. Treated right hilar mass and right hilar and subcarinal nodes stable compared with January. Right adrenal nodule stable. No new pulmonary nodule, effusion or new lesion in the chest, abdomen or pelvis. Centrilobular emphysema. Right chest port in place.

documents.title: Oncology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Dear Doctor,

Follow-up for Ms. Whitney, extensive-stage small cell lung cancer on maintenance atezolizumab 1680 mg every 4 weeks since 11/04/2025.

Interval: admitted 03/07-03/12 with symptomatic hyponatremia from SIADH (Na 120), corrected slowly with hypertonic saline; now on sodium chloride tablets and a fluid restriction, with Na 133 on your 04/13 labs - thank you for following this closely. TSH and AM cortisol were normal during the admission.

Restaging CT 04/17/2026 shows the response maintained, with nothing new; January's scan was also stable.

She looks well today. Plan: continue maintenance atezolizumab, next restaging in about 3 months. Please continue managing the sodium; we are happy to discuss if it falls again.

Medications reviewed: tiotropium, fluticasone propionate, albuterol PRN, ondansetron PRN, sodium chloride 1 g TID. NKDA.

Medical Oncology

documents.title: Medicare Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV, delayed from January by the winter's events.

Function: independent in ADLs; daughter now does the big grocery run, Irene manages the rest. Still drives short distances in daylight. No falls since discharge. PHQ-9 = 4. Cognition: Mini-Cog 5/5, back to her usual.

Meds reviewed and current: tiotropium 18 mcg daily, fluticasone propionate 250 mcg BID, albuterol PRN, ondansetron PRN (rarely now), sodium chloride 1 g TID, atezolizumab q4wk at the cancer center.

Screening: mammogram - stopping routine screening given her cancer and goals, she agrees. Colon - not pursuing. Lung screening - replaced by oncology's restaging CTs. Bone density 2023 normal.
Vaccines: fall flu and COVID 2025 done; PCV20, RSV, Shingrix, Tdap complete.

Advance care planning (~20 min, daughter present): Talked through the March admission. She still wants full treatment. Daughter remains HCP. She'd like to go over longer-term wishes with oncology too; we'll pick this up again in the fall.

Exam: lungs diminished, no wheeze, no crackles. RRR. No edema. Port site clean.

Plan: CMP, CBC, lipids today. Continue salt tabs + 1 L restriction. COPD/sodium visit in July.

documents.title: Follow-up - COPD, SIADH, SCLC
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Summer has been quiet. Breathing at her baseline - albuterol 2-3x/wk, more on the muggy days. No flares since December. Atezolizumab every 4 wks continues. Restaging CT in July - per Irene, oncology said "no change"; no letter yet. Taking salt tablets with meals and keeping to about a liter. Thinking clear, no headaches, no falls.

O: Vitals per flowsheet. Alert, oriented, good humor. Lungs diminished throughout, no wheeze, no crackles. RRR. No edema. Port site clean.

A/P
1. SIADH - stable on sodium chloride 1 g TID + 1 L restriction. BMP today.
2. COPD GOLD 3 - stable on tiotropium + fluticasone + PRN albuterol. Refills current.
3. ES-SCLC - maintenance atezolizumab, July restaging reportedly stable; will request the report.
4. Fall vaccines: flu and COVID when available, coordinate with infusion days.
RTC 5 wks.

Addendum 16:05: Na 133. Portal message sent - no changes.
